_comment: SafeClick Phase 3 declarative rule definitions. Migrates Phase 2 heuristics to a JSON-configurable format. Phase 6 org admins can add/modify rules without a code deploy. Each rule uses structured conditions — never eval()/exec().

rules.name: URL Too Long
rules.description: Flags URLs longer than 100 characters — phishers hide the real domain in long paths.

rules.name: High Subdomain Entropy
rules.description: Random-looking subdomains (entropy > 3.5) are generated by phishing kits.

rules.name: High Path Entropy
rules.description: Random-looking path segments indicate phishing kit generation.

rules.name: Raw IP Address
rules.description: Legitimate services use domain names, not raw IP addresses.

rules.name: @ Symbol Obfuscation
rules.description: The @ symbol in URLs makes browsers navigate to the part after @, hiding the real destination.

rules.name: Excessive Subdomain Depth
rules.description: More than 3 subdomain levels is unusual for legitimate sites.

rules.name: Excessive Hyphens in Domain
rules.description: Many hyphens in a domain are characteristic of phishing URLs that try to mimic brands.

rules.name: Brand Keyword in Wrong Domain
rules.description: A known brand name appearing in the subdomain or path but not in the registered domain is a strong impersonation signal.

rules.name: Multiple Brand Keywords
rules.description: Multiple brand keywords in a single URL is rare for legitimate sites.

rules.name: Phishing Action Words
rules.description: Action words like login/verify/confirm/update combined with brand keywords is a classic phishing pattern.

rules.name: Suspicious Encoding
rules.description: Double-encoded percent sequences or null bytes indicate obfuscation attempts.

rules.name: IDN / Punycode Domain
rules.description: Internationalized domain names using punycode are used in homograph attacks to visually mimic legitimate brands.

rules.name: Suspicious Free/Cheap TLD
rules.description: Free or very cheap TLDs (.tk, .ml, .ga, .cf, .xyz, etc.) are disproportionately used in phishing.

rules.name: Suspicious TLD + Brand Keyword
rules.description: A cheap/free TLD combined with a brand keyword in the domain is a very strong phishing indicator.

rules.name: Non-Standard Port
rules.description: Legitimate public services rarely use non-standard ports (not 80/443).

rules.name: No HTTPS
rules.description: HTTP (not HTTPS) for a site that collects credentials is a risk factor.
